heads.text: TO ARMS! WHERE ARE THE ARMS?

caps.text: The invading horde. The artist ran out of room after four goblins and implies the rest.
Goblins at the gate, seen from the safety of the artist's bedroom.
A troll, drawn from memory. The memory was brief and mostly screaming.
Our brave militia, depicted as three circles and an axe. Accuracy disputed by the militia.
The drawbridge, shown raised, which it was not at the time.
Artist's impression of the siege. The smudge is either a war beast or a thumb.
The enemy banner. The artist could not spell the insults on it, so drew a frowning face.
Defenders on the wall. One is the artist's cousin, drawn larger out of loyalty.

reps.text: Lookouts report a dark mass on the horizon carrying spears, torches and a strong sense of entitlement. Citizens are urged to go inside and stay inside, which most were doing anyway.
The mayor has responded by declaring the matter 'a military problem' and returning to his office to admire his collection of chests.
Militia commanders confirm the barracks are ready, the weapons are sharp, and the soldiers are mostly asleep. A bell will be rung loudly until this changes.
Witnesses describe the attackers as 'goblin-shaped, but angrier.' Several haulers have refused to fetch stones from the riverbank until further notice.
{who} was first to spot the invaders and has been granted the honour of standing nearest to them. {first} described the honour as 'an honour', quietly.
Food stores are believed sufficient to last the siege provided nobody eats. The bookkeeper is recounting the plump helmets for the third time this morning.
Traders camped outside the walls are reportedly reconsidering their life choices. The goblins have already reconsidered the traders' wagons, and taken them.
Experts estimate the siege will end in one of two ways: victory, or a very interesting chapter in somebody else's history book. Losing, as ever, remains fun.
Residents of {fort} are reminded that the cage traps by the entrance are not seating, however tired one may be after fleeing.

kickers.text: The goblins were asked for comment and replied with arrows.
Siege coverage continues on page 4, if page 4 survives.
Please do not open the gate to ask them questions.

heads.text: DO NOT PET THE NEW ARRIVAL

caps.text: The beast, to scale. The artist was asked to use a bigger page and declined.
Artist's impression. The beast has six legs, or possibly the artist's pen slipped twice.
Our correspondent drew this while running. It shows.
The creature breathing something. The artist assumes fire but lists 'gas, webs, or opinions'.
A dwarf for scale. The dwarf has since asked to be removed from the drawing.
This is the beast's good side. It does not have a good side.
The artist says the eyes followed him around the room. There are eleven of them.
Drawn from a description shouted through a closed door.

reps.text: Survivors describe the creature as 'enormous, wrong, and smelling of old cave cheese.' Hauling is suspended in all corridors with the word 'deep' in their name.
The beast's arrival has prompted the fortress to rediscover the lever that seals the cavern. Nobody remembers which lever. There are forty levers.
Scholars note the creature was forgotten for centuries and are now trying very hard to forget it again. Early results are not promising.
{who} reportedly saw the beast first and offered it a mug of ale in the interest of diplomacy. The mug has not been returned.
The militia captain says the squad is 'ready to engage,' then asked where exactly the creature was, then asked to be excused for the afternoon.
Animal experts confirm it is not a carp, though they refuse to rule out the possibility that it is somehow worse than a carp.
The beast has no official name yet. Proposed names include 'The Thing', 'The Other Thing', and 'Please Go Away Now'.
Citizens of {fort} are asked to stop throwing socks at the creature. It does not want socks. It has made that very clear.

kickers.text: The beast declined to be interviewed and ate the notepad.
Our natural history pullout has been postponed indefinitely.
{first} is said to be 'considering a career in surface farming.'

heads.text: GONE TO THE GREAT HALL BELOW
DEATH IN THE FORT: CATS SUSPECT

caps.text: Mourners at the graveside. The artist apologises for the hands.
The deceased as we remember them: a circle on a stick, holding a mug.
Artist's impression of the afterlife. Lots of ale. The artist admits this is wishful.
The coffin. The artist drew it very carefully, then drew the lid upside down.
A cat looking guilty. The cat was not involved. The artist simply likes drawing cats.
The memorial slab, drawn before the engraver finished, so it just says 'HERE LIES'.
Friends gather to remember. Several are only there for the wake ale.
The artist tried to draw a solemn face and produced a potato. We regret the potato.

reps.text: Friends remember {first} as stubborn, loyal, and only occasionally on fire. A slab will be engraved as soon as somebody remembers where the mason went.
The fortress observed a respectful moment of silence, which ended when someone dropped a barrel of plump helmets down the stairs.
Colleagues describe the deceased as a hard worker who hated elves, loved ale, and once hauled a single sock across the entire map.
The bookkeeper has updated the population ledger with a heavy sigh. The cats have been questioned and released without charge.
A coffin has been ordered from the carpenter, who has eleven coffins already and 'just had a feeling.' Mourners are advised to bring their own mugs.
Grief counsellors remind citizens that tantrums in the memorial hall are strongly discouraged, however strong the feelings and however empty the ale barrels.
{first}'s belongings, including a stone mug, a bone earring and a strong opinion about carp, will be distributed according to tradition: whoever grabs first.
The chief medical dwarf states nothing could have been done, then added that, actually, several things could have been done, and wandered off.
Authorities urge all citizens of {fort} to drink something, eat something, and avoid standing near anything that looks hungry, sharp or deep.

kickers.text: {first} could not be reached for comment.
The family requests no carp.
Flowers may be left at the slab, once there is a slab.
The obituary continues on page 9, which does not exist.

heads.text: FORT IN MOURNING FOR GOOD BOY
A PAW PRINT ON OUR HEARTS
NOT THE DOG! (OR CAT. OR YAK.)

caps.text: The late animal, drawn with four legs. The artist checked. Twice.
Artist's impression of the pet. The artist was not sure what species it was and hedged.
The animal's favourite spot, a pile of socks, recreated faithfully.
A tiny grave with a tiny slab. The artist cried and smudged the ink.
The owner, weeping. The tears are the size of the owner's head. Artistic licence.
The other cats, attending the funeral for the free food.
This is either a dog or a very fluffy war hammer. The artist will not say.
The pet in happier times, chasing a vermin the artist forgot to draw.

reps.text: The animal is remembered for its loyalty, its warmth, and its habit of sleeping in the dining hall exactly where everyone wanted to walk.
Its owner, {who}, has taken the news badly and is said to be one bad meal away from a full tantrum. Friends are bringing ale.
The fortress cats have issued no statement but were seen eating from the deceased's food bowl within the hour.
A small memorial is planned near the kennels. The mason has agreed to engrave it with a picture of the animal, or of a carp, depending on mood.
Animal handlers confirm the creature lived a full life, by which they mean it ate, slept, and once bit a noble, which everyone secretly enjoyed.
Children of the fortress have been told the animal has gone to live on a big farm on the surface, where the sky is large and frightening.
The loss leaves {fort} with {pop} citizens and one fewer warm thing to put your feet on during the long winter.
Veterinary science, such as it is, has been consulted and confirms the animal is 'definitely not getting up again, sorry.'

kickers.text: The animal has no comment, and never did.
Please do not adopt another one until the paperwork is done.
{first} has asked for privacy and a puppy.

caps.text: The tantrum in progress. The artist drew the angry eyebrows first and ran out of face.
Artist's impression of a thrown table. The table is airborne. So is the artist's dignity.
The dwarf's face, drawn from a safe distance of two corridors.
A broken door. The artist says it was a nice door and is upset about it personally.
Bystanders fleeing. They are drawn as dots because they were very fast.
The cause of the tantrum, allegedly: a slightly wet sock.
The artist has drawn steam coming out of the ears. Witnesses confirm this is accurate.
Some furniture before and after. The 'after' is just a scribble.

reps.text: Witnesses say the outburst began over a missing mug and quickly escalated to include doors, a statue, and the entire concept of hauling.
{who} was last seen punching a cabinet and demanding to speak to whoever designed the bedrooms. The designer is in hiding.
Counsellors list the likely causes as no ale, rain on the surface, a dead friend, sleeping on the floor, and being looked at by an elf.
The sheriff has been notified and is putting on his boots. He is putting them on very, very slowly.
Citizens are reminded that when a dwarf is upset, the correct response is to offer ale and then stand well behind a locked door.
Damage so far includes two tables, a chair, a cat's pride, and the mood of everyone in the meeting hall.
The nobles have responded by asking for a better dining room, which is widely believed to be what started all this.
Doctors confirm that {first} is physically fine, emotionally a volcano, and should not be handed anything heavy for at least a season.

kickers.text: {first} declined to comment and threw the reporter's chair.
The dining hall will reopen once it has furniture again.
Have you tried ale? Try ale.

caps.text: The dwarf, staring into the middle distance. The artist drew the middle distance, too.
A list of demands pinned to the workshop door. The artist could only read 'SHELLS?'
Artist's impression of genius: a small cloud with a lightning bolt in it. Close enough.
The locked workshop. The artist pressed an ear to the door and drew what he heard: humming.
The materials requested, drawn as question marks because nobody knows what they are.
Eyes very wide. The artist used an entire pot of ink on the pupils.
Fellow citizens backing politely away. The artist drew everyone backing away from himself, too.
The workshop chimney, puffing ominously. Smoke shaped like a sock was not intended.

reps.text: Witnesses report the dwarf rose from dinner, muttered about 'the shape of it,' and walked into the nearest workshop without finishing the ale, which alarmed everyone.
{who} has posted a scribbled list of required materials. Haulers can find the stone and the wood but are unsure what 'the bones of something proud' means.
Experts warn that a moody dwarf without the right materials may go insane, so please check the stockpiles, the refuse pile, and under the beds.
The workshop has been claimed, the door is shut, and the forge is roaring. Other craftsdwarves were asked to find something else to do. They chose drinking.
Nobody knows what is being made. Theories include a crown, a cage, a spoon of terrible beauty, or another very expensive sock.
The mayor has asked to be informed the moment it is finished, so he can demand it for his bedroom and be refused.
Friends say {first} has not spoken in two days except to whisper 'more' at the door. The cats now sit outside it in a semicircle.
Residents of {fort} are asked to avoid knocking, singing nearby, or asking 'is it done yet.' It is not done yet.

kickers.text: We will report the result, or the screaming, whichever comes first.
{first} could not be reached; the door is locked.
Do not offer the moody dwarf a carp. Trust us.

caps.text: The artifact. The artist got ten seconds to look at it before the mayor took it away.
The artifact's engraving, which is itself an image of a dwarf drawing an artifact.
The item glows in this drawing. It does not glow in real life. The artist wanted it to.
The creator holding the artifact aloft. The arms are different lengths. So is the artifact.
Detail of the menacing spikes. There were spikes. There are always spikes.
The artifact on display. The guards beside it are drawn as two angry triangles.
We believe this is a crown. The artist believes it is a hat. They have stopped speaking.
The artifact with a halo of sparkles, added at the request of the craftsdwarf.

reps.text: After days locked in the workshop, the dwarf emerged with a legendary creation decorated with spikes, images of carp, and an engraving of itself being decorated.
{who} has named the item something nobody can pronounce, and the bookkeeper has already valued it at more than the entire fortress, including the fortress.
The mayor asked to keep it in his bedroom. The creator said no. It was the first time anyone has said no to the mayor, and it was wonderful.
Scholars agree the artifact will be remembered for generations, mainly because elves will come asking for it and we will tell them no.
The creation is said to be menacing with spikes of bone and encircled with bands of something sparkly. The haulers are nervous about carrying it.
Citizens may view the artifact in the hall, provided they do not touch it, breathe on it, or attempt to drink from it, even if it is a mug.
{first} has reportedly returned to normal life and asked for a long nap and a very large ale, both of which have been granted.
This latest treasure raises the fortress's wealth considerably, which experts warn is exactly the sort of thing goblins like to read about.

kickers.text: The artifact remains silent, as is its right.
Elves who ask about it will be told it is a rock.
Viewing hours are whenever the guards are asleep.

caps.text: The masterpiece, drawn badly so the craftsdwarf feels even better by contrast.
Artist's impression of perfect craftsmanship. The artist is not a craftsdwarf.
The craftsdwarf, glowing with pride. The glow is an ale stain.
The item from three angles. All three angles look like a boot.
Little stars around the object to show it is good. The artist believes stars are a quality mark.
The workshop afterwards. The artist drew a tidy room, which was a lie.
Rival craftsdwarves in the background, drawn small and jealous.
The finished piece, with an arrow helpfully labelled 'GOOD'.

reps.text: Colleagues describe the piece as flawless, balanced and 'annoyingly good,' and have asked that the creator stop showing it to them at mealtimes.
{who} reportedly gazed at the finished piece for some time, then announced it was 'quite nice,' which for a dwarf is a speech of thunderous emotion.
The item has been sent to the stockpile, where it will sit beside forty crude stone mugs and make them all feel terrible.
Traders are expected to offer handsomely for it. The craftsdwarf has said it is not for sale, then said it is for sale, then cried.
The fortress expects a modest happy thought for the creator and a much less modest increase in boasting at the tavern.
Experts say the piece shows a mastery unseen in {fort} since, frankly, the last masterpiece, which was on a Tuesday.
The nobles have requested one each. The craftsdwarf has requested that the nobles go and find a large hole.
{first} credits the success to hard work, good ale, and the absence of anybody wandering in to ask where the socks are kept.

kickers.text: The piece is on display until somebody hauls it somewhere stupid.
{first} will be signing autographs. Nobody can read.
Rival craftsdwarves are 'happy for them.' They are not.

heads.text: WE DUG TOO DEEP? WE DUG JUST RIGHT

caps.text: The vein of ore, as described by the miner: 'like that, but shinier.'
Artist's impression of the discovery. The rock is grey. The artist only had grey.
A miner pointing excitedly. The pick is bigger than the miner, as is traditional.
The newly opened cavern. It is a black square. The artist insists that is what it looked like.
Cross-section of the mine. Please ignore the small figure falling down the shaft.
Sparkles indicate value. The artist uses sparkles generously and without evidence.
The miners celebrating. One is holding a mug. They are all holding mugs.
A mushroom tree in the cavern. The artist has never seen a tree and guessed.

reps.text: Miners report the find with tremendous excitement, followed by a request for more pickaxes, more ale and fewer questions about how deep they have gone.
{who} struck the discovery mid-swing and shouted 'Strike the earth!' even though, technically, the earth had already been struck many times.
Economists predict the find will double the fortress's wealth, triple the nobles' demands and quadruple the number of goblins who suddenly want to visit.
The bookkeeper has been asked to count the new riches but has instead gone to lie down. 'It's too many,' he said, faintly.
Experts warn that what lies further below may be magma, glory, or something that has been waiting very patiently. Digging will continue anyway.
Smelters are reportedly ecstatic, which in a smelter looks like a slight nod. Their furnaces have been stoked accordingly.
Residents of {fort} are asked not to go and look at it all at once, as the corridor down there is narrow and the floor is optional.
{first} has been offered a bonus of one roasted plump helmet, which was accepted with tears of gratitude.

kickers.text: Don't dig straight down. We say this every issue.
The deep rock had no comment, but glittered suggestively.
Further digging is scheduled, as is further regret.

heads.text: MORE DWARVES, SAME AMOUNT OF ALE

caps.text: The new arrivals. The artist got bored after five and drew the rest as a crowd-shaped cloud.
Migrants entering the fort. All of them are looking at the ale stockpile.
Artist's impression of their luggage: nothing. They brought nothing.
A migrant who claims to be a legendary cheesemaker. A cheese is drawn for context.
The welcome committee: one dwarf, waving, and a cat, not waving.
The newcomers' first look at the bedrooms. The artist drew their expressions carefully.
A child migrant holding a sock. Nobody knows whose sock.
Migrants as dots on the horizon. It was a long way and the artist was in a hurry.

reps.text: The new arrivals bring a wealth of skills, including fishing, more fishing, cheese making, and in one case 'thinking about stones.'
Housing officials confirm there are not enough beds and have suggested the migrants 'share' or 'sleep standing up like horses.'
The population of {fort} now stands at {pop}, a number the kitchen staff described, after a long pause, as 'oh no.'
Every newcomer has been assigned to hauling, which they all accepted in the traditional manner, by refusing and going to the tavern.
Officials report the migrants left their old homes due to goblins, boredom, and a rumour that we have very good ale. The rumour is false.
{who} was among the new arrivals and has already claimed a bedroom that belonged to someone else, which bodes well for integration.
Long-term residents are asked to be welcoming, to share their mugs, and to stop telling newcomers about the carp.
Several migrants appear to be nobles in waiting. Citizens are urged to remain calm and hide the good chairs immediately.

kickers.text: Welcome to {fort}. Please wipe your boots.
{first} has already asked where the ale is kept.
Orientation is at dawn. Attendance is optional and nobody will attend.

heads.text: THEY WANT OUR MUGS, OF COURSE

caps.text: The caravan. The wagon has three wheels in this drawing and four in real life.
Artist's impression of a trader. The hat was larger than this. Much larger.
The depot, drawn just before the haulers ignored it entirely.
A pack animal looking unimpressed. The artist got the expression right first time.
Goods on display. The artist could not identify any of them and drew blobs.
The broker haggling. The speech bubble just says 'NO.'
If these are elves, the artist has drawn them as trees. That is a political statement.
The trade ledger, drawn as a very long scroll, because it was.

reps.text: Traders arrived bearing cloth, leather, exotic cheeses and a single barrel of something labelled 'probably food.' The depot has been cleared for haggling.
The fortress broker is preparing to trade forty stone mugs for one dog, a deal that has worked every time and that nobody should question.
Haulers are reminded that goods must be carried to the depot before trading, a fact they have so far met with a collective shrug.
Merchants say the road was long and dangerous, which is apparently why everything costs three times what it should.
If the caravan is elven, citizens are asked not to offer them anything made of wood. This rule is strictly enforced and wildly enjoyed.
{who} volunteered to negotiate and was promptly talked into buying a bag of sand. Training continues.
The arrival of new goods has caused great excitement in {fort}, particularly over the cloth, which can be made into more socks.
The traders have politely requested that the cats stop climbing into their wagons. The cats have politely refused.

kickers.text: Prices are non-negotiable, except when they are negotiated.
The caravan leaves soon. Hide the cat.
No refunds. No elves. No exceptions.

caps.text: The baby. It is a circle. Babies are circles, says the artist.
The proud parent. The artist forgot to draw the baby, then remembered, then drew it small.
A tiny pickaxe, gifted at birth. Tradition. Dangerous tradition.
The nursery, also known as the corridor outside the dining hall.
The baby's first mug. The artist insists this is a real custom.
Proud relatives. One is holding the baby upside down. The artist did not invent this.
The baby, drawn with a beard because the artist cannot imagine a dwarf without one.
Everyone cooing. The cat is not cooing. The cat is evaluating.

reps.text: The newborn is reported to be healthy, loud, and already gripping things like a hammer. The parents describe the child as 'a little Urist.'
{who} welcomed the child into the world, which in this case is a rock tunnel with a nice view of a moat.
The fortress population now stands at {pop}, and the child has already been assigned to hauling, effective in roughly twelve years.
Relatives gathered to admire the infant and offer advice, most of it about carp, all of it wrong.
Doctors confirm the baby has all the usual parts and a very strong opinion about being put down.
The child will be given a name by the parents and a nickname by the tavern, and it is the second one that will stick.
Older citizens of {fort} recall when they too were tiny and loud, and then went straight back to being large and loud.
Nobles have requested the baby be kept away from their quarters. The baby has requested nothing, being a baby.

kickers.text: The baby's official statement was mostly gurgling.
{first} is accepting gifts. Socks preferred.
Congratulations. The sleepless nights begin now.

caps.text: The happy couple. The artist made them hold hands, which took four attempts.
Artist's impression of love. It is a heart shape. The artist is not subtle.
The ceremony, held in the dining hall between lunch and other lunch.
The rings, carved from bone. The artist drew them slightly too large, like bracelets.
Guests applauding. One guest is asleep on the table, faithfully recorded.
The newlyweds' shared bedroom: one bed and a chest. Romance.
Two beards entwined. The artist is proud of this and should not be.
The cake, which was a plump helmet with a candle in it.

reps.text: The couple met while hauling the same stone in opposite directions, and friends say it was love at first argument.
{who} has married after a long courtship consisting mainly of sitting near each other at dinner and not speaking.
The ceremony was brief, heartfelt, and interrupted by a cat chasing vermin down the aisle, which guests agreed was the best part.
The newlyweds will share a bedroom, a cabinet, and, in a historic step, a single mug. Witnesses wept openly.
Gifts included two stone mugs, a sock of unusual quality, and a strongly worded note from the mayor asking for less noise.
Love is in the air of {fort} this {season}, along with dust, smoke and the faint smell of the refuse pile.
Experts say the union strengthens the fortress, mainly because two dwarves in love are less likely to throw tables.
{first} described the day as 'fine,' a word which, in dwarven, means 'I am overwhelmed with joy and need a drink.'

kickers.text: The couple asked for privacy and a bigger bed.
{first} has requested no carp-themed gifts.
Congratulations, and please stop kissing in the corridors.

heads.text: THE DEAD WALK. ALSO THEY FLOAT.

caps.text: The ghost. The artist drew a sheet with holes, then admitted ghosts here wear no sheets.
Artist's impression of being haunted. The artist's hand was shaking. So were the lines.
The spectre gliding through a wall. The wall was drawn second, which makes this harder.
A cold spot, shown with shivering lines, as we have no blue ink.
The ghost in life, for comparison. The artist says the ghost looks better now.
Terrified citizens. Their hair is standing up. Their beards are standing up.
The missing memorial slab, drawn as an empty space with an arrow. This is the problem.
The ghost frowning at the artist. The artist drew himself running away.

reps.text: Witnesses report a translucent figure drifting through the dining hall, moaning about unfinished business and the quality of the ale.
{who} has returned as a restless spirit, apparently because nobody got around to carving a memorial. The mason has been sent for. Again.
The ghost has been seen moving objects, frightening the cats, and in one case rearranging the stockpile more efficiently than the living.
Priests recommend an engraved slab or a proper burial. The bookkeeper recommends a slab, as it is cheaper.
Citizens of {fort} are reminded that ghosts cannot be hauled, traded, or assigned to a squad. We have checked all three.
Experts say the dead return when they are unhappy. Considering the bedrooms, experts are surprised there are not more of them.
Friends say {first} was always one to linger, especially at the tavern, so this behaviour is described as 'very on brand.'
Several dwarves have been badly frightened and are now refusing to work, which management notes is also what they did before.

kickers.text: The ghost was reached for comment, but only said 'Woooo.'
Engrave a slab. Please. For everyone's sake.
{first} remains unavailable, yet somehow everywhere.

heads.text: THE CEILING IS NOW THE FLOOR

caps.text: The cave-in. The artist drew lots of rocks, then more rocks, then gave up and drew dust.
Artist's impression of the ceiling before and after. 'After' is lower.
A miner looking up at the exact wrong moment, with a question mark above him.
The rubble pile. Several boots can be seen. The artist hopes they are just boots.
Dust clouds, drawn as scribbles. The artist coughed throughout.
The missing support pillar, shown with an arrow and the word 'OOPS'.
A dwarf holding up a tiny rock, as if that would help.
Rescue workers digging. They are smiling because the artist cannot draw worried.

reps.text: A section of ceiling decided it had been a ceiling long enough and became a floor instead, bringing a great deal of rock along for the change.
Engineers believe the collapse was caused by someone removing the last support, despite a very clear sign reading 'DO NOT REMOVE LAST SUPPORT.'
Rescue teams are clearing rubble and asking everyone to stand somewhere else, anywhere else, preferably under a lot of very solid rock.
{who} was nearby when it happened and reports feeling 'a rumble, a gust, and then extremely surprised, in that order.'
The architect has denied responsibility, blamed the miners, blamed the stone, and finally blamed the elves, which went down well.
Officials remind citizens of {fort} that dust is not ale, even if it is in a mug and you are very thirsty.
The fallen stone will be hauled away and turned into blocks, mugs and, inevitably, a brand new ceiling.
Survivors described the noise as louder than a siege and slightly quieter than the dining hall on ale day.

kickers.text: The ceiling declined to apologise.
Please consult a mason before removing anything holding anything up.
Our offices have relocated slightly downward.

caps.text: The soldier in a heroic pose. The axe is very big and the soldier very pleased.
Artist's impression of martial mastery: a dwarf, a sword, and some motion lines.
The training dummy, depicted with an expression of total defeat.
The barracks, drawn as one bed and forty weapon racks, which is accurate.
The soldier's muscles. The artist was told 'more' and kept going.
Fellow soldiers saluting. One salutes with the wrong hand. The artist was that soldier.
The champion's armour, with a dent where the artist ran out of ink.
A worried goblin in the background. Any resemblance to a real goblin is coincidental.

reps.text: After seasons of hitting the training dummy, the dummy has formally conceded, and the soldier has been recognised as a true master of arms.
{who} celebrated by sparring with three comrades at once, winning, and then asking everyone to watch it happen again.
Military commanders say the fortress is now considerably safer, provided the threat arrives near the barracks and during duty hours.
Goblin spies are believed to have taken note, and several goblins have reportedly reconsidered their plans for this {season}.
The champion has been awarded an extra mug of ale and a chair, which in the barracks counts as a parade.
Fellow soldiers describe the champion as fearless, disciplined, and absolutely unbearable at dinner every single night.
Citizens of {fort} are reminded that a master of arms is a soldier, not a hauler, and should not be asked to carry stones.
{first} credits the success to daily training, a strict diet of plump helmets, and an unresolved grudge against an elf.

kickers.text: The training dummy has requested a transfer.
{first} is available for sparring, unfortunately for you.
Goblins are advised to consult page 4 before attacking.
